label: PF Backlog 434
title: B4: OEM / white-label profiles (no forks)

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend the existing validation profiles system (`/api/v1/validation/profiles` API and `config/validation-profiles.json`) into a generalised OEM/white-label profile mechanism. Add a new configuration layer (e.g. `config/oem-profiles.json`) that overlays branding metadata, feature flags, API branding, and default validation profiles per OEM partner. The existing profile API becomes one facet of the OEM profile. No fork of code; all customisation is configuration-driven. Reuse the existing profile resolution logic and parameterise it with an OEM context (org_id, partner_slug).
dependency_findings: REQUIRES BI-PF-0391 (Epic B) at least in PARTIAL state — OEM profiles are one sub-item of the epic and need the epic's architecture decisions (config layer, gateway) to be agreed.
RELATED BI-PF-0388 (compiled editions) — OEM builds may use the compiled-artifact pipeline; profile overlay must work in compiled-Python runtime.
BLOCKS nothing yet; may BLOCK future OEM-specific integration items.
conflict_findings: Low conflict risk — only module touched is config and a new API route. No other grooming item in this batch touches config/validation-profiles.json.
BI-PF-0402 (persistence adapters) may add config surfaces; coordinate config-file ownership.
duplication_findings: No existing OEM/white-label feature found in the codebase — this is genuinely new capability within existing infrastructure.
config/validation-profiles.json is a precedent for config-driven behaviour; OEM profiles generalise this pattern rather than duplicate it.
BI-PF-0391 (EPIC B editions) covers OEM in its scope; ensure no overlap with edition-gating logic.
analysis.rationale: The item has a clear direction (no forks, config-driven) and existing code to extend. Gaps are in the concrete OEM customisation matrix and runtime identity resolution, which a human must decide. Architecture fits cleanly as an extension of the existing validation-profile pattern.
assumptions: OEM deployment is a single-binary/config overlay, not a code fork (per item title).
Existing profile resolution can accept an OEM context parameter without breaking current callers.
OEM customisation needs are limited to branding metadata, feature gating, and default profiles in v1.
risks: Scope creep: OEM profile may attempt to cover too many customisation axes (branding, behaviour, licensing) before a concrete OEM deal demands them.
Config-layer explosion: adding an OEM overlay on top of validation profiles could create deep nesting or confusing precedence rules.
No concrete OEM partner requirements yet; risk of over-engineering for hypothetical needs.
evidence: Candidate code shows /api/v1/validation/profiles and config/validation-profiles.json already exist as config-driven extension points.
Item body confirms trigger is 'OEM deal' — a concrete business signal.
BI-PF-0388 ADR settles on config-driven editions.
missing_info: What specific OEM customisation axes are needed in v1? (branding only? licensing? feature gates?)
How is OEM identity resolved at runtime? (env var? config key? JWT claim?)
What is the precedence order when OEM profile conflicts with user-selected profile?
Is there a concrete OEM partner timeline that sets urgency?

missing: Concrete OEM customisation matrix for v1
context_review.reason: Existing profile infrastructure provides a clear extension point. The gaps are product-level decisions (what to customise, how to identify OEM) that do not block technical design.
